relevance_note: Case report of a girl with Blau syndrome/EOS and a NOD2 variant inherited from her asymptomatic father: "A novel C483W NOD2 mutation was identify in the proband and her asymptomatic father."
method_note: Built by hand-written Python from my own reading; no tables in the paper. In scope: the proband ('patient', rule 5), her asymptomatic carrier father and her tested-negative mother (rule 2 labels), and the R334W Blau syndrome patient used as a positive control in the functional assays ('unnamed person 1'; described with a NOD2 variant, a BS diagnosis and assay results; no clinical details). Healthy controls (n = 3) are out of scope. The mother has no variant row (variant not found). Age at onset uses the earliest symptom (rash since 6 months); joint lumps since age 3 recorded as a feature onset. Age at last evaluation is the age at referral (9 years); no age at diagnosis stated. Country not recorded: Taiwan is named only for the immunization schedule and the Taiwan Biobank, not as origin. Fever checklist left not reported because the paper excludes only 'prolong fever or fever without source' (narrower). Tenosynovitis checklist left not reported: ultrasound shows 'synovial hyperplasia surrounding extensor tendons' but the paper never calls it tenosynovitis for the proband (the Discussion mentions tenosynovitis only generally). 'Levels of complements C3, C4 ... were all negative' is ambiguous for complement and was not recorded as a feature; HLA-B27 negativity is a genotype and was not recorded. Chest radiography negative recorded as written (intra-thoracic lesions excluded); it does not exclude interstitial lung disease. Father: 'lacks clinical BS/EOS phenotype' and 'asymptomatic' are whole-phenotype statements, so his checklist stays not reported. Variant type not stated for C483W (only R334W/R334Q are called missense), so 'not reported'. Transcript and protein for the father's row come from sentences about the same exact variant. R334W protein-only string recorded as printed without a 'p.' prefix. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: emollients and topical steroid for skin lesions; oral methotrexate 10 mg/m^2/week; oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day; adalimumab
span: Emollients and topical steroid were prescribed for the control of her skin lesions with limited effect.
Oral methotrexate at a dose of 10 mg/m^2/week was prescribed for the control of her arthritis but the swelling and inflammation continues to progress.
Additional treatment with 1 mg/kg/day of oral prednisolone greatly mitigated the rashes, but its effect on arthritis control was not satisfying.
Adalimumab, a monoclonal antibody against TNF-α, was prescribed 5 months following her initial treatment with noticeable improvement.

functional_evidence_statement.value: HEK293T NFκB reporter assay: gain-of-function; NFκB autoactivation in proband CD11b+ cells (20.5% p-NFκB+/CD11b+); elevated plasma IL-6 and TNF-α
span: The results supported that the C483W mutation was confirmed to be a gain-of-function mutation.
NFκB autoactivation was observed in the CD11b^+ cells of the symptomatic proband harboring NOD2 C483W mutant
The p-NFκB^+/CD11b^+ cells account for 20.5%, 10.9%, 0.9%, 5.1% and 28.1% of all CD11b^+ cells in the proband, her father, mother, healthy controls and the BS/EOS control, respectively.
the level of plasma cytokines IL-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) were also elevated in the proband
our data supported the pathogenicity of C483W NOD2 mutation underlining BS/EOS with incomplete penetrance
the C483W mutation was confirmed to be a gain-of-function mutation
